title: What UVM's built-in measurements count and what the Overview, Risk and Remediation History dashboards show

prose.label: Ticket measurements.
prose.text: {{ticket-open-counts}} {{closed-measures}} {{sla-measures}} {{time-to}} Mean Time to Remediate {{divergence:mttr-definition}}. Total Open Tickets {{divergence:open-tickets-definition}}. Total Tickets Over SLA {{divergence:tickets-over-sla-scope}}.

customization.statement: Additional measurements can be added on request and default measurement calculations can be overridden by contacting the Zscaler Account team.

quotes: Additional measurements can be added upon request, and default measurements' calculations can be overridden according to specific needs. Contact your Zscaler Account team for more details.

ticket-open-counts.statement: The measurement terminology article defines Total Open Tickets as tickets that are Active or Inactive and not in the Closed bucket, and Active Tickets (Open) as only Active tickets not in the Closed bucket, excluding inactive ones.

quotes: The number of tickets set as Active or Inactive that are not in the Closed bucket.
The number of tickets set as Active that are not in the Closed bucket. This measurement does not include inactive tickets.

sla-measures.statement: The measurement terminology article defines Total Tickets Over SLA as treating a ticket not in the Closed bucket as over SLA when the set date range is after its SLA, and a Closed-bucket ticket as over SLA when it was moved to Closed after the SLA date.

quotes: For tickets not in the Closed bucket, over SLA is considered when the set date range is after the set SLA for the ticket. For tickets in the Closed bucket, over SLA is considered when the date the ticket was moved to the Closed bucket was after the set SLA date.

closed-measures.statement: Closed Tickets counts only tickets set to the Closed bucket within the date range, whereas Total Closed Tickets includes tickets closed before the range.

quotes: The number of tickets in the Closed bucket in the set date range. This includes tickets closed before the set date range.
This measurement only counts tickets that were set to the Closed bucket within the set date range; tickets closed prior to the set date range are not counted.

pct-measures.statement: The measurement terminology article defines the percentage measurements as % Remediation = Inactive findings / Total findings, % Total Tickets Over SLA = Tickets Over SLA / Total Tickets, and % Open Tickets Over SLA = Open Tickets Over SLA / Total Open Tickets.

quotes: | % Remediation | Inactive findings / Total findings |
| % Total Tickets Over SLA | Tickets Over SLA / Total Tickets |
| % Open Tickets Over SLA | Open Tickets Over SLA / Total Open Tickets |

time-to.statement: Ticket Mean Time to Remediate runs from ticket creation to the date the ticket state last turned Inactive, Mean Time to Assign to the first time the assignee became not null, and Mean Time to Close to the ticket's status bucket being Closed, all in days.

quotes: | Ticket Mean Time to Remediate | The average number of days it takes for a ticket to turn inactive. This measurement counts the days passed from the ticket's creation date up to the date the ticket's state turned Inactive. | Ticket Create Date | Ticket State last turned to Inactive | Day |

| Ticket Mean Time to Assign | The average number of days it takes for a ticket to be assigned. This measurement counts the days passed from the ticket's creation date up to the date the ticket's assignee is changed from Null for the first time. | Ticket Create Date | Ticket Assignee first turned to Not null | Day |

| Ticket Mean Time to Close | The average number of days it takes for a ticket to be closed. This measurement counts the days passed from the ticket's creation date up to the date the ticket's state turned Closed. | Ticket Create Date | Ticket's status bucket is Closed | Day |

finding-measures.statement: New Findings counts findings first seen in the date range and excludes reopened findings, Detected Findings counts findings that turned Active in the range, and Active Findings is a unique count by finding key on the last day of the range.

quotes: The number of findings first seen in the set date range. This measurement does not include reopened findings.
The number of findings that turned Active during the set date range.
The number of active findings on the last day of the set date range. This is a unique count by finding key.

asset-measures.statement: Vulnerable Assets counts the assets linked to Active findings on the last day of the date range, and Risk Mass is the sum of severity scores of the Active findings of a ticket or asset.

quotes: The number of assets linked to Active findings on the last day of the set date range.
The sum of all severity scores of the Active findings associated with an entity (ticket or asset).

overview-dashboard.statement: The Overview dashboard displays source findings and source assets for each of the data sources configured in the account, after mapping but before unification; UVM merges the same vulnerability on the same machine reported by different sources into a single unified record, so the central Findings node might show a lower number than the sum of raw source findings; the trend arrow shows the percentage change in deduplicated findings in the past 30 days, and the flow includes the findings to tickets ratio.

quotes: On the left, the dashboard displays source findings and source assets for each of the data sources configured in your account (e.g., Qualys, CrowdStrike, ServiceNow), after mapping but before unification.
Thus, you might see a lower number in the central Findings node than the sum of all raw source findings on the left.
including the findings to tickets ratio.
UVM identifies when multiple different sources report the same vulnerability on the same machine and merges them into a single, unified record.
The trend arrow indicates the percentage of increased or decreased deduplicated findings in the past 30 days.

overview-tiles.statement: The Overview dashboard has a Vulnerable Assets tile (unique unified assets with at least one active finding), a Total Unique CVE tile, a % Assigned Tickets tile (currently active tickets assigned to an owner or team) and a % Third-Party Tickets tile (tickets dispatched through outegrations).

quotes: The Vulnerable Assets tile displays the total number of unique, unified assets in your environment that have at least one active finding.
The Total Unique CVE tile counts the number of distinct Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) identifiers currently active across your environment.
The % Assigned Tickets tile tracks how many currently active tickets have been assigned to a specific owner or remediation team.
The % Third-Party Tickets tile represents the percentage of tickets that have been dispatched to an external work management system using outegrations (e.g., Jira or ServiceNow).

overview-mttr.statement: The Overview dashboard's Tickets by Severity section says the Mean Time to Remediate (MTTR) measurement shows the average number of days it takes for a ticket to move from opened to resolved.

quotes: The Mean Time to Remediate (MTTR) measurement shows the average number of days it takes for a ticket to move from opened to resolved.

rh-key-metrics.statement: The Remediation History dashboard's Key Metrics Over Time chart describes Total Open Tickets as tickets that were open at some point during the period regardless of state, Total Tickets Over SLA as open tickets past their SLA date at some point during the period, and % Open Tickets Over SLA as relative to the total number of tickets.

quotes: Open tickets here refer to tickets that were in a status bucket but not tagged as Closed.
Total Open Tickets: The number of tickets that were open at some point during the specified time period (regardless of their state).
Total Tickets Over SLA: The number of open tickets that are past their SLA date at some point during the specified time period (can be Active or Inactive).
% Open Tickets Over SLA: The percentage of open tickets that were past their SLA date at some point during the specified time period, relative to the total number of tickets.

risk-methods.statement: The Risk dashboard offers three risk scoring methods, chosen from the Risk Scoring Method drop-down: AVG Risk (average severity score of the entity's findings), Max Risk (highest severity score) and Risk Mass (sum of severity scores of the active findings).

quotes: AVG Risk: Calculates the average severity score of findings associated with the entity.
Max Risk: Returns the highest severity score related to the entity.
Risk Mass: Calculates the sum of all severity scores of the active findings associated with the entity.
You can select your preferred method from the Risk Scoring Method drop-down menu at the top right of the dashboard.

risk-charts.statement: The Risk dashboard's Key Metrics Over Time chart shows the last 6 months with Active Findings as the default measurement and up to two measurements at a time, and the dashboard exports as a PDF.

quotes: This chart shows the historical data over the last 6 months. The default measurement shown in the following chart is Active Findings
You can add up to two measurements to the chart at a time by clicking the + icon.
You can export the dashboard as a PDF by clicking the Export icon at the top right of the dashboard.

risk-weekly.statement: The Risk dashboard's Findings - Last Week widget counts Discovered findings (became active in the last 7 days and are active currently) and Undetected findings (active and undetected in the last 7 days).

quotes: The number of findings that became active in the last 7 days and are active currently.
The number of findings that were active and undetected in the last 7 days.

remediation-history.statement: The Remediation History dashboard's top-panel tiles show current open tickets by severity and are not affected by the time filter; ticket measurement titles including Open refer to ticket status and those including Active to ticket state.

quotes: Each tile shows the current number of open tickets in your account based on severity level
This data does not reflect any historical data, and is not affected by the time filter.
ticket measurement titles that include Open refer to ticket status, while those that include Active refer to ticket state.

remediation-limits.statement: The Key Metrics Over Time chart of the Remediation History dashboard is limited to 8 metrics; the Open Tickets by Current Status chart omits Closed-tagged buckets and empty buckets; Analyze Remediation Work defaults to grouping by assignee and exports as CSV, and the dashboard exports as PDF.

quotes: The selection of measurements is limited to 8 metrics.
status buckets tagged as Closed in your ticket status settings aren't displayed. Status buckets without any associated tickets aren't displayed in this chart.
By default, the chart displays data based on the assignee.
you can also export this chart as a CSV by clicking the Export icon.
You can also Export the dashboard as a PDF by clicking the Export icon at the top of the dashboard.

mttr-definition.summary: The Overview dashboard says MTTR is the average days for a ticket to move from opened to resolved, while the terminology article defines Ticket Mean Time to Remediate as the days from ticket creation until the ticket state last turned Inactive.

positions.says: MTTR is the average number of days for a ticket to move from opened to resolved.

quotes: The Mean Time to Remediate (MTTR) measurement shows the average number of days it takes for a ticket to move from opened to resolved.

positions.says: Ticket Mean Time to Remediate counts days from the ticket's creation date to the date its state last turned Inactive.

quotes: | Ticket Mean Time to Remediate | The average number of days it takes for a ticket to turn inactive. This measurement counts the days passed from the ticket's creation date up to the date the ticket's state turned Inactive. | Ticket Create Date | Ticket State last turned to Inactive | Day |

mttr-definition.impact: The two pages do not name the same start and end points for MTTR; state which page a figure follows.

open-tickets-definition.summary: The terminology article defines Total Open Tickets as Active or Inactive tickets not in the Closed bucket, while the Remediation History page defines it as tickets that were open at some point during the period regardless of state.

positions.says: Total Open Tickets is the number of tickets set as Active or Inactive that are not in the Closed bucket.

quotes: The number of tickets set as Active or Inactive that are not in the Closed bucket.

positions.says: Total Open Tickets is the number of tickets that were open at some point during the specified period, regardless of state.

quotes: Total Open Tickets: The number of tickets that were open at some point during the specified time period (regardless of their state).

open-tickets-definition.impact: A count labelled Total Open Tickets can follow either definition depending on the page; state which page a figure follows.

open-over-sla-pct.summary: The terminology article defines % Open Tickets Over SLA as Open Tickets Over SLA / Total Open Tickets, while the Remediation History page says it is relative to the total number of tickets.

positions.says: % Open Tickets Over SLA = Open Tickets Over SLA / Total Open Tickets.

quotes: | % Open Tickets Over SLA | Open Tickets Over SLA / Total Open Tickets |

positions.says: % Open Tickets Over SLA is the percentage of open tickets past their SLA date at some point in the period, relative to the total number of tickets.

quotes: % Open Tickets Over SLA: The percentage of open tickets that were past their SLA date at some point during the specified time period, relative to the total number of tickets.

open-over-sla-pct.impact: The denominators differ between the two pages (Total Open Tickets versus total number of tickets); state which page a figure follows.

tickets-over-sla-scope.summary: The terminology article defines Total Tickets Over SLA over both open and Closed-bucket tickets, while the Remediation History Key Metrics chart describes it as open tickets past their SLA date.

positions.says: Total Tickets Over SLA covers tickets not in the Closed bucket and tickets in the Closed bucket.

quotes: For tickets not in the Closed bucket, over SLA is considered when the set date range is after the set SLA for the ticket. For tickets in the Closed bucket, over SLA is considered when the date the ticket was moved to the Closed bucket was after the set SLA date.

positions.says: Total Tickets Over SLA is the number of open tickets past their SLA date at some point in the period.

quotes: Total Tickets Over SLA: The number of open tickets that are past their SLA date at some point during the specified time period (can be Active or Inactive).

tickets-over-sla-scope.impact: Whether Closed-bucket tickets count toward Total Tickets Over SLA depends on the page; state which page a figure follows.
